q: Which tone is written with no mark in the romanization?
why: The mid tone has no mark: maa. Every other tone has one.

q: ม้า (horse) is máa. Which tone is that?
why: The acute mark (á) shows the high tone.

q: Which romanization means near?
why: Near is glâi, with a falling tone. glai, with no mark, is mid: far.

q: What does a doubled vowel such as aa show?
why: A doubled vowel is held longer; length is part of the word.

q: In khǎo maa mǎi (Is he coming?), what does your voice do on mǎi?
o: It says the word's own rising tone
It goes up extra high, as in English
It drops to a low tone
It stays flat with no tone
why: ไหม has its own rising tone; you do not add an English question rise.
ไกล (glai) has a mid tone; glâi with a falling tone means near.
Rice (khâao) has a falling tone; white (khǎao) has a rising tone and a long vowel. khǎo is he.
Horse is máa, with a high tone; mǎa with a rising tone is a dog.
Near has a falling tone: glâi. glai, mid, is far.
Dog is mǎa, with a rising tone: it dips, then rises.
White is khǎao: rising tone, long vowel.

p: Type the romanization of ม้า (horse)
hint: high tone · use the accent bar
why: ม้า (máa) has a high tone; หมา (mǎa) with a rising tone is a dog.

p: Type the romanization of ใกล้ (near)
hint: falling tone · gl + ai
why: ใกล้ (glâi) has a falling tone; with a mid tone, glai means far.

p: Type the romanization of หมา (dog)
hint: rising tone · long aa
why: หมา (mǎa) has a rising tone; máa with a high tone is a horse.

q: Which of these starts with a puff of air?
why: ph, th, kh and ch have a puff of air; bp, dt and g have none.

q: Which word means egg?
why: Egg is khài, with a puff of air. gài, with no puff, is a chicken.

q: How do you say ภูเก็ต (Phuket)?
o: with a p and a puff of air, never f
with an f, as in English
why: Thai ph is a p with a puff of air, never f.

q: How should the k at the end of นก (bird) sound?
o: held, with no burst of air
a clear k with a puff of air
why: Final k, t and p are held: you stop the sound, with no release.

q: How do you start the word งู (snake)?
o: with ng, as in the middle of singing
why: Thai words can start with ng: say singing and drop the si.
ดู (duu) has a long vowel; ดุ (dù), with a short vowel, means to scold.
Far is glai, with a mid tone; glâi, with a falling tone, means near.
Chicken is gài, with no puff of air; khài, with a puff, is an egg.
To look is duu, with a long vowel; dù is short.
Far has a mid tone, so it has no mark: glai.
Chicken is gài: no puff of air and a low tone.

p: Type the romanization of ข้าว (rice)
hint: falling tone · long aa + o
why: ข้าว (khâao) has a falling tone and a long vowel; ขาว (khǎao) is white.

p: Type the romanization of ดุ (to scold)
hint: short vowel · low tone
why: ดู (duu) has a long vowel; ดุ (dù) is short.

p: Type the romanization of ไข่ (egg)
hint: kh: a k with a puff of air · ai
why: ไข่ starts with kh, a k with a puff of air; gài, with no puff, is a chicken.

q: Which is the romanization of ค่ะ (female speaker, in a statement)?
why: ค่ะ has a falling tone: khâ. khá, with a high tone, is the question form.

q: A woman asks How are you? Which ending is right?
why: A woman's question ends in คะ; a man's ends in ครับ.

q: You bump into someone. What do you say?
why: ขอโทษ is sorry, and also excuse me.

q: Which is the everyday way to say goodbye when you leave?
why: People say ไปก่อนนะ or สวัสดี when leaving; ลาก่อน sounds like a final farewell.

q: Which word goes before a first name as a polite title?
why: คุณ + first name, as in คุณมาลี, for men and women.
In a statement ค่ะ has a falling tone; คะ with a high tone is for questions.
A question ends in คะ, with a high tone; ค่ะ, with a falling tone, ends statements.
A man ends with ครับ, even after a long phrase; ค่ะ is what women say.
A woman ends a statement with ค่ะ, falling; คะ is for questions.
After ไหม a woman uses คะ, with a high tone.
ไม่เป็นไร means it's OK or never mind.

hint: ขอบคุณ (khàawp-khun) · มาก (mâak) · ค่ะ (khâ)
why: A statement ends in ค่ะ, with a falling tone; คะ, with a high tone, asks a question.

hint: สบาย (sà-baai) · ดี (dii) · ไหม (mǎi) · ครับ (khráp)
why: ไหม (mǎi) with a rising tone asks the question; ไม่ (mâi), with a falling tone, means not.

hint: สวัสดี (sà-wàt-dii) · ครับ (khráp)
why: A man ends with ครับ; ค่ะ is what women say.

q: Which is the romanization of สอง (two)?
why: สอง has a rising tone: sǎawng.

q: How do you say 20?
why: 20 is ยี่สิบ, not สองสิบ.

q: How do you say 21?
why: The 1 at the end of a bigger number is เอ็ด.

q: A price tag says 50 บาท. How do you read it?
why: Read the digits as one Thai number: 50 is ห้าสิบ.

q: What is หมื่น?
why: Thai has its own word for 10,000: หมื่น. แสน is 100,000.
ห้า (hâa, five) has a falling tone; หา (hǎa) with a rising tone means to look for.
เก้า (gâao, nine) has a falling tone and a long vowel; เก่า (gào) means old.
Twenty is ยี่สิบ, never สองสิบ, and บาท comes after the number.
Nine is เก้า, falling and long; เก่า means old.
A 1 at the end of a bigger number is เอ็ด.
เท่าไร (how much) goes at the end; it needs no ไหม.

hint: เก้าสิบ (gâao-sìp) · บาท (bàat)
why: เก้า (gâao) has a falling tone and a long vowel; เก่า (gào) means old.

hint: ห้าร้อย (hâa-ráawi) · บาท (bàat)
why: ห้า (hâa) has a falling tone; หา (hǎa), with a rising tone, means to look for.

hint: เท่าไร (thâo-rai) or เท่าไหร่ (thâo-rài) · คะ (khá)
why: A question ends in คะ, with a high tone; ค่ะ is for statements.

q: Which is the romanization of ขา (leg)?
why: ข is high class, so ขา has a rising tone: khǎa.

q: Which letter is mid class?
why: The mid-class letters are ก จ ด ต บ ป อ.

q: Which letter has the same sound as ส?
why: ส and ซ both sound s: ส is high class, ซ is low class.

q: Which letter sounds bp, with no puff of air?
why: ป is bp, with no puff; พ and ผ are ph, with a puff; บ is a plain b.

q: What does อ do at the start of a syllable?
o: It is silent and holds the vowel
why: อ at the start is silent: อาหาร starts straight on the vowel.
ข is a high-class consonant, so ขา has a rising tone.
ส is a high-class consonant, so สวย has a rising tone; with a mid tone it means unlucky.
A letter's name is its sound plus aaw, then a word: ก ไก่, g as in chicken.
ข is high class: ขา has a rising tone.

p: the letter g, as in chicken
why: ไก่ starts with ก, so its letter name is ก ไก่.

p: the letter kh, as in buffalo
why: ควาย starts with the low-class ค, the kh letter used in ค ควาย.

p: Type the romanization of ขา (leg)
hint: kh · long aa · high class
why: ข is a high-class consonant: with a long vowel and no tone mark it gives a rising tone.

p: Type the romanization of สวย (pretty)
hint: s · uuai · high class
why: ส is a high-class consonant, so สวย has a rising tone; said with a mid tone it is ซวย, unlucky.

p: Type the romanization of the letter ข and its name word
hint: kh + aaw · then the word egg
why: Its name is ข ไข่: kh plus aaw, then the word for egg.

q: Which word is khâo (to enter)?
why: เข้า has a short vowel; ข้าว, with a long vowel, is rice.

q: Where is the vowel written in ดู (to look)?
why: ู sits below the consonant: ดู.

q: Which word has a vowel written before its consonant?
why: แ is written before ม, but you say m first: mâae.

q: Which two vowel signs sound the same?
why: ใ and ไ both sound ai; only about twenty words use ใ.

q: In เรือ (boat), how many vowels are there?
o: none: เรือ has only consonants
why: เ, ื and อ together make one vowel, uuea.
เข้า (khâo) has a short vowel; ข้าว, with a long vowel, is rice.
ดู (duu) has a long vowel; ดุ, with a short vowel, means to scold.
ใหม่ (mài, low tone) means new, and it comes after the noun.
เข้า has a short vowel; ข้าว, long, is rice.
Rice is ข้าว: long vowel, falling tone.
New is ใหม่, with a low tone; ไม่ is not.

hint: กิน (gin) · ข้าว (khâao)
why: ข้าว has a long vowel; เข้า, with a short vowel, means to enter.

hint: ดู (duu) · หมา (mǎa)
why: ดู has a long vowel; ดุ, with a short vowel, means to scold.

p: Type the romanization of เรือ (boat)
hint: one vowel in three pieces: เ ื อ
why: เรือ is one vowel, uuea, written around ร: เ before, ื above, อ after.

q: Which word is khǎo (he, she)?
why: เขา has a short vowel and a rising tone; ข้าว (rice) and ขาว (white) are long.

q: A man says I. Which word does he use?
why: ผม is a man's polite I; ฉัน and ดิฉัน are for women.

q: Which means my friend (female speaker)?
why: The owner follows the noun, and a woman's I is ฉัน.

q: Who would you call พี่?
o: someone a little older than you
why: พี่ is an older sibling, and also you for anyone a bit older.

q: Someone asks if you are going. Which short answer sounds natural (male speaker)?
why: Once it is clear who you mean, Thai drops the pronoun.
The owner comes after the noun: เพื่อนผม.
The owner comes after the noun: พี่ชายฉัน.
เขา (khǎo) has a rising tone and a short vowel; ข้าว, falling and long, is rice.
A man's I is ผม, and it follows the noun.
He or she is เขา: short vowel, rising tone.
A woman ends a statement with ค่ะ; คะ is for questions.

hint: พี่สาว (phîi-sǎao) · ฉัน (chǎn)
why: The owner comes after the noun: พี่สาวฉัน.

hint: น้องชาย (náawng-chaai) · ผม (phǒm)
why: The owner comes after the noun: น้องชายผม.

hint: เรา (rao) · ไป (bpai) · ครับ (khráp)
why: A man ends with ครับ, whoever the subject is; ค่ะ is what women say.

q: Which is the romanization of รัก (to love)?
why: รัก is low class, dead and short, so it has a high tone: rák.

q: Which final sound does รถ (car) end with?
why: ถ at the end of a syllable is a held t.

q: Which syllable is live?
why: คน ends in n, so it is live; the others end in k, t or p.

q: จาก (from) has a mid-class letter and ends in k. Which tone does it have?
why: Mid class + dead syllable gives a low tone.

q: How do you end the word นก (bird)?
o: hold the k with no burst of air
release the k with a puff
add a short vowel after the k
why: Final k, t and p are held, never released.

ใกล้ (glâi) has a falling tone; ไกล, with a mid tone, means far.
A dead syllable on a mid-class letter takes a low tone: จาก (jàak).
Low class, dead, short vowel: a high tone, rák.
Near is ใกล้, with a falling tone; ไกล is far.
From is จาก: mid class, dead syllable, low tone.

p: Type the romanization of จาก (from)
hint: j · long aa · final k
why: A dead syllable on a mid-class letter takes a low tone: จาก (jàak).

p: Type the romanization of ราก (root)

p: Type the romanization of อาหาร (food)
